body.title: bug: pushing to a protected branch with the automatic Actions token fails with a 500, and the Actions user cannot be allowed to push
body.body:
### Can you reproduce the bug on the Forgejo test instance?

No, I can't try it on the test instance for some reason

### Description

A workflow that pushes to a protected branch with the automatic token
(`GITHUB_TOKEN` / `FORGEJO_TOKEN`) is rejected with an internal server error,
whatever the branch protection settings:

    remote: Forgejo: Internal Server Error (no message for end users)
     ! [remote rejected] HEAD -> develop (pre-receive hook declined)

Server log:

    routers/private/hook_pre_receive.go: preReceiveBranch() [E] Unable to GetUserByID
    for commits from <old> to <new> in <Repository>: user does not exist [uid: -2, name: ]

### Cause

In `routers/private/hook_pre_receive.go`, step "5. Check if the doer is allowed
to push" calls `user_model.GetUserByID(ctx, ctx.opts.UserID)`. With the automatic
token the user ID is `ActionsUserID` (-2), which has no row in the database, so
the lookup fails and the hook answers 500.

The same file already handles this user elsewhere
(`if ctx.opts.UserID == user_model.ActionsUserID { ctx.user = user_model.NewActionsUser() }`),
but not in the branch protection check. The code is identical on the `forgejo`
branch today.

### Two problems

1. **A 500 instead of an answer.** The push should either be accepted or be
   refused with "Not allowed to push to protected branch", never fail with an
   internal error that says nothing to the user.
2. **No supported way to let a workflow push to a protected branch with the
   automatic token.** Branch protection can allow users, teams and deploy keys,
   but not the Actions user. A release workflow that commits version bumps back
   to its branch therefore has to choose between removing the branch protection
   and storing a long-lived credential of a real account or a deploy key. Both
   weaken what the automatic token is meant to provide: a short-lived credential
   scoped to one repository.

### Expected

1. The pre-receive hook handles `ActionsUserID` in the branch protection check
   and never answers 500 for it.
2. Branch protection offers an explicit option to allow pushes made with the
   automatic Actions token (like "allow deploy keys with write access"), off by
   default.

### Reproduction

1. Protect a branch (any settings).
2. Run a workflow on that branch which commits a file and runs
   `git push origin HEAD:<branch>` after a plain `actions/checkout`.
3. The push fails with the output above.

### Related

#11159 reported the same error and was closed by its author after switching to
a personal access token. The underlying defect was not addressed.

### Forgejo Version

15.0.11 (also reported on 14.0.x and 16.0.2 in #11159)

### How are you running Forgejo?

Official container image, not built by us: `codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo:15`
(reports `15.0.11+gitea-1.22.0`), the default rootful variant, with the
image's own entrypoint.

It runs on Kubernetes v1.35 as a single-replica Deployment written as plain
manifests (no Helm chart), on arm64 nodes (Ubuntu 24.04, containerd 2.2).
Configuration is passed through `FORGEJO__section__KEY` environment
variables. Database: SQLite.

Actions jobs run on Forgejo Runner v13.2.1 (`data.forgejo.org/forgejo/runner:13`),
ephemeral runners in the same cluster with a Docker-in-Docker sidecar.

### Logs

Here are the logs of one occurrence (Forgejo 15.0.11, official image
`codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo:15`, runner v13.2.1, `actions/checkout@v4`).
Repository, host names and IP addresses are replaced.

**Server log** — the push is authenticated, the pre-receive hook fails:

    2026/11/14 17:25:33 ...eb/routing/logger.go:109:func1() [I] router: completed GET /<owner>/<repo>/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack for <runner>, 200 OK in 7.2ms @ repo/githttp.go:509(repo.GetInfoRefs)
    2026/11/14 17:25:33 ...eb/routing/logger.go:109:func1() [I] router: completed POST /<owner>/<repo>/git-upload-pack for <runner>, 200 OK in 7.7ms @ repo/githttp.go:469(repo.ServiceUploadPack)
    2026/11/14 17:25:33 ...eb/routing/logger.go:109:func1() [I] router: completed GET /<owner>/<repo>/info/refs?service=git-receive-pack for <runner>, 200 OK in 8.1ms @ repo/githttp.go:509(repo.GetInfoRefs)
    2026/11/14 17:25:33 .../hook_pre_receive.go:368:preReceiveBranch() [E] Unable to GetUserByID for commits from eb3e37ca84eb84dd520306ea3706ae5f5adb66bc to e6bc0ba38621c495f1b046872841a12a9435ce2d in <Repository 2:<owner>/<repo>>: user does not exist [uid: -2, name: ]
    2026/11/14 17:25:33 ...eb/routing/logger.go:109:func1() [I] router: completed POST /api/internal/hook/pre-receive/<owner>/<repo> for 127.0.0.1:0, 500 Internal Server Error in 3.7ms @ private/hook_pre_receive.go:202(private.HookPreReceive)
    2026/11/14 17:25:33 ...eb/routing/logger.go:109:func1() [I] router: completed POST /<owner>/<repo>/git-receive-pack for <runner>, 200 OK in 155.8ms @ repo/githttp.go:477(repo.ServiceReceivePack)

**Job log** — same second, client side:

    [develop e6bc0ba] chore: release versions & update hashes [skip ci]
     8 files changed, 32 insertions(+), 22 deletions(-)
    remote:
    remote: Forgejo: Internal Server Error (no message for end users)
    remote:
    To http://<forge>:3000/<owner>/<repo>
     ! [remote rejected] HEAD -> develop (pre-receive hook declined)
    error: failed to push some refs to 'http://<forge>:3000/<owner>/<repo>'

**Workflow** — a plain checkout, so git uses the automatic token; no other
credential is configured anywhere in the job:

    on:
      push:
        branches: [develop]
    jobs:
      publish:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              fetch-depth: 0
          - run: |
              # ...changes files...
              git add -A
              git commit --no-verify -m "chore: release versions & update hashes [skip ci]"
              git push --no-verify origin "HEAD:${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

**Branch protection of `develop`**: <à compléter : push autorisé ou restreint,
liste blanche, « appliquer aux administrateurs », approbations requises…>

The failure does not depend on those settings: the lookup at
`hook_pre_receive.go:368` runs for any protected branch as soon as the push
does not come from a deploy key. The same workflow pushes without error to an
unprotected branch.

### Database

SQLite

body.title: problem: API: incorrect response status codes for issue subscriptions
body.body:
### Does your problem still exist on the latest Forgejo version?

Yes, the problem still exists (tested on a next instance)

### About your usage of Forgejo

Interacted with the following two API endpoints:

- `PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{index}/subscriptions/{user}` (operation `issueAddSubscription`)
- `DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{index}/subscriptions/{user}` (operation `issueDeleteSubscription`)

### Problem description

The Forgejo API returns status code **403** (_Forbidden_) when the user is not authorized to modify other user's issue subscriptions: https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/src/commit/16c6241def58eb90312c4aceac1924eda657daac/routers/api/v1/repo/issue_subscription.go#L123-L127

However, the documentation mentions a **304** (_Not Modified_) status code for both operations ([issueAddSubscription](https://v18.next.forgejo.org/api/swagger#/issue/issueAddSubscription) and [issueDeleteSubscription](https://v18.next.forgejo.org/api/swagger#/issue/issueDeleteSubscription)) instead.

Additionally, the description of the error message (_for both operations_) is a bit confusing/misleading:  

> User can only subscribe itself if he is no admin

Even though the server responds with this error when a _non-admin_ user attempts to manipulate other user's subscriptions.

### Potential workarounds

Adjust the response status codes of both operations under the `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{index}/subscriptions/{user}` path.

### Forgejo Version

18.0.0-dev-283-7aa74e4f83+gitea-1.22.0.

Reproducible up until 16c6241def58eb90312c4aceac1924eda657daac.

### Solutions

*Accepted solutions to address this problem will go here*

body.title: problem: allow matrix webhooks to not show link previews
body.body:
### Does your problem still exist on the latest Forgejo version?

Unknown, I can't try it for some reason (please explain)

### About your usage of Forgejo

we are hosting https://git.sable.moe and we have a webhook for our issues.

### Problem description

we have tons of repo activity and it creates a lot of link preview spam. this makes our chats hard to read in our matrix rooms.

### Potential workarounds

as per [MSC4095: Bundled URL Previews](https://github.com/matrix-org/matrix-spec-proposals/pull/4095), a message can indicate that it should not have a link preview fetched.

```json
{
  "type": "m.room.message",
  "content": {
    "msgtype": "m.text",
    "body": "https://matrix.org",
    "m.url_previews": [],
    "m.mentions": {}
  }
}
```

### Forgejo Version

17.0.1-dotgay+gitea-1.22.0

### Other details about your environment (software names and versions)

unsure what would be useful here. we are running a soft fork of forgejo, https://git.gay/gitgay/forgejo, but this behavior should be changed upstream and not there.

### Solutions

*Accepted solutions to address this problem will go here*
